policy_floor.rule: Classic rewarded ads must only be shown after an affirmative, unambiguous user opt-in.
Disclose the required action and the reward, clearly and conspicuously, before every single rewarded-ad instance.
The ad must be skippable/dismissible; never force interaction to completion.
Never offer direct monetary (cash or cash-equivalent) rewards, under any circumstance.
Declining or skipping must not impede or degrade normal app use.
Deliver the promised reward once the required action is actually completed.
Rewarded interstitials run on an opt-out model: show an intro screen announcing the reward with a skip option, rather than requiring a prior opt-in tap.
If a rewarded ad unlocks in-app content/currency that also has a paid purchase path, that paid path must go through platform in-app purchase (Apple), not a custom unlock mechanism.
Incentivizing users to watch an ad or complete an in-app action is allowed on iOS; incentivizing ratings, reviews, or app-store actions (installs) is not, and neither can be forced for access.
Never gate app functionality on ATT tracking consent, and never incentivize giving that consent, for ad targeting purposes.
Kids Category apps (Apple) must carry no third-party advertising or analytics at all; child-directed apps on Android must follow the Families Ads and Monetization Policy.
On a child-directed property, verifiable parental consent gates both personal-data collection and, depending on what the ad network collects, whether ad networks may run at all.
Google Play's general disruptive-ads / unexpected-placement restrictions (including the ~15-second non-closeable cap) are waived specifically for genuine opt-in rewarded ad units.
Grant the reward immediately client-side for UX, but reconcile every grant against a signed server-to-server callback before treating it as final; this is anti-fraud infrastructure, not a UX nicety.
policy_floor.applies_to: rewarded (all networks with SSV support: AdMob, AppLovin MAX, Unity)

policy_floor.rule: Design the reward trigger around a discrete, completed action (an ad view, a specific task) rather than raw accumulated engagement or screen time — the latter is the exact pattern EU regulators forced off the market for minors'-mental-health/addictive-design reasons (historical, program withdrawn).
policy_floor.applies_to: any engagement-reward design, EU market especially

format_differences.notes: User-initiated; must be an affirmative, unambiguous opt-in before the ad shows; skippable; no direct monetary reward.
Shown automatically at natural app transitions, not user-initiated; opt-out model via an intro screen that announces the reward and lets the user skip.
No primary AdMob rewarded-specific policy text found naming app-open ads as a reward-capable format; treated as out of scope / gap, not asserted either way.

No primary AdMob/AppLovin/Unity policy page found that names 'offerwall' specifically; typically a mediation/third-party SDK surface (a list of multiple reward offers) rather than a native single-network ad-unit type. Flagged as a gap.
